text: Prof. Ansel Okafor led the excavation at Tel Maridun, according to a statement released Tuesday by the Maridun Antiquities Council. The regional dig, carried out over six weeks on the eastern ridge above the old quarry road, uncovered a sealed storeroom containing pottery, bronze tools and three inscribed clay seals. Council archaeologist Lena Voss said the team had identified the work area as part of a larger settlement layer dating to the late Fourth Century era. “This season’s trench gave us our clearest view yet of the site’s administrative quarter,” Voss said. Officials said the excavation involved 18 researchers and students from the university in Port Sable. The artifacts are now being catalogued for public display later this year.
